review_notes: Scope: retain the full piecewise-linear accrual family in Tables 3–5: CF, DD, and Jones accrual specifications; three book proxies and the abnormal-return proxy individually (Tables 3–4); the three book/market proxy pairings and all-proxy combination (Table 5); and both pooled full-sample and repeated three-digit-SIC industry fits. The central source question is how accruals asymmetrically recognize timely gains/losses, and the paper states that it reports evidence on all proxies individually and in combinations (physical PDF pp. 1, 8, 12–20). Table 1 is the conventional linear replication/benchmark and Table 2 reports proxy overlap; these do not estimate the new piecewise baseline. Later time-trend, robustness, subgroup, and future-cash-flow analyses address extensions outside this one principal family.

The actual estimator for the Table 3–5 regressions is not identified; method is null and flagged in every model. For DD fits, the paper does not specify whether lagged and lead cash flows use average assets of their own years or year t; formula fields remain null and the timing gap is flagged. Industry-specific N values in tables are counts of qualifying fits, not per-fit observation counts; sample_size is null for those models.

In Table 4 and the combined Table 5 fits, the specific note names continuous accounting variables for annual tail deletion; treatment of abnormal-return tails is not separately stated in that note, while the general sample description states annual tail exclusions for each variable. This source detail is preserved without asserting an incompatible rule.

In Table 5 Panel D Jones columns, the table reports no standalone CF_t coefficient row while reporting DCF_t × CF_t. The RHS inventory follows the printed column; the omission rationale is not separately identified beyond the paper’s general collinearity note.
descriptive_reason: Targeted search of the complete assigned paper text for descriptive/summary statistics and summary terms related to retained variables (including means, standard deviations, minima/maxima, medians, percentiles, and variable names) found no data-value summaries for the selected baseline outcomes, predictors, raw inputs, or components. Table 1 is a linear benchmark outside the retained family; Table 2 reports proxy correlations and chi-square tests, which are not variable descriptives; later results concern additional or robustness analyses. Table notes reporting coefficient means and average observations per industry are fit summaries, not data-variable descriptives.
results_review_notes: All 48 frozen baseline result sets from Tables 3–5 were compared with the selected original table cells, including intercepts, all predictor estimates and parenthetical statistics; parameter identities and frozen RHS links were reviewed.

The source labels industry-specific parentheticals as t-statistics based on the cross-sectional coefficient distribution; Student-t is used with df unknown and that dispersion is not treated as a sampling SE. Pooled parenthetical cells are not labeled t or z and retain kind other with test context/reference unknown.

No coefficient standard errors, exact coefficient p-values, significance markers, or significance legend are printed for Tables 3–5. Each selected fit now includes source-printed No. of obs. and Adj. R² (%) as explicit auxiliary rows.

Jones-model intercepts remain on the printed scale with unit multiplier, consistent with the later source explanation; Table 5 Panel D individual coefficients carry the source multicollinearity caution.
